Overview

  • Western Australia: A mouse plague is under way across multiple regions. The worst outbreak is occurring north of Geraldton in the “WA Northern” agro-ecological zone, followed by another east from Fitzgerald in the “WA Sandplain”. With crops maturing, consider baiting before grain fill, as zinc phosphide becomes less effective once grain develops on the head. Mouse abundance in WA Eastern and Central zones appears to be low, but growers should remain vigilant.

  • Adelaide Plains, Yorke & Eyre Peninsulas (SA): We have seen a decrease in mouse activity on the Adelaide Plains due to low food availaiblity and proactive management prior to sowing. Moderate mouse numbers still remain however, which could increase as more food is becoming available. Continue monitoring as crops mature, and be ready to act before grain fill if activity increases.

  • An emergency permit has been issued by the APVMA for the higher dose ZnP50 bait: see GRDC website for details.

  • Elsewhere (Mallee & Wimmera (Vic/SA), Victoria & southern/central NSW and Northern NSW & southern Queensland), mouse numbers likely remain low.

Management recomendations

  1. Monitor crops for signs of mouse activity using chew cards or a walk-through of crops.

  2. Where mouse damage is evident in maturing crops, apply zinc phosphide bait before grain fill — once grain has developed on the head, mice are less likely to take ZnP bait. ZnP25 is the only currently registered bait available; use in accordance with the label instructions and report any adverse effects via the APVMA website. There is currently an emergency permit for the higher dose ZnP50 bait, administered through GRDC. Locations this permit applies to changes on a fortnightly basis based on recent monitoring led by GRDC, check current access on the GRDC website.

  3. Plan for a clean harvest (minimal grain loss) to reduce mouse food carry over into next season, and control weeds and grasses along fence lines and crop margins before seed set.

About

Mouse forecasts are enabled through a Grains Research and Development Corporation and CSIRO investment into the 2025-29 Mouse Monitoring and Surveillance project via the Rodent Pest Management team. Forecasts will be updated seasonally or as new data comes available.

We are actively developing new statistical models to improve mouse forecasts, and working on their presentation. This work is run in coordination with the National Mouse Group, a grower-led network of farmers, industry representatives, state government, GRDC and CSIRO. The group meet three times a year to update local reports of the current mouse situation, review management recommendations and determine research priorities.

Monitoring data

Mouse population surveys are conducted 2 - 3 times a year at each of the ~170 long-term monitoring sites. Mice are surveyed through active burrow searches and chewcards. To calibrate this data against more robust population density measurements, we conduct live-trapping at 3 sites (Adelaide Plains SA, Northern Mallee VIC and Central West NSW).

Mouse monitoring data is collected by CSIRO, NSW Local Land Services, NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development, Central West Farming Services, Birchip Cropping Group, & Farmanco. We particularly thank NSW DPIRD who generously provide additional live-trapping survey data. Further live-trapping data is also occasionally supplied through the GRDC / CSIRO Mouse Ecology 2024-2029 project.

We also receive reports from farmers, agronomists and other community members directly. This is key information we consider given we cannot feasibly survey every paddock across the entire grain growing region.

Report mouse activity

You can quickly report sightings of mice on your farm on MouseAlert.

We incorporate citizen observations with our scientific surveys to create these forecasts and improve our understanding of mouse populations. We are primarily using observations of mice within paddocks (not houses or sheds). Please don’t only report observations of high mouse activity, if you’ve looked and found no sign or low mouse activity, this information is just as important to record!
